result.title: ElasticDino: Dense Semantic Features Using Elastic Deformations
result.summary: Vision transformers (ViTs) serve as the backbone for countless vision tasks, including dense prediction tasks, such as segmentation and depth estimation, even though the quadratic complexity of self-attention severely limits feature resolution and induces spatial artifacts. In this work, we introduce ElasticDino, a lightweight adapter which produces high-resolution feature maps, adhering to the fine details of the input image. As a key insight, we observe the consistency of artifacts across channels, and simultaneously resolve them to match the input image structure. Using a slim architecture based on spatial deformations, ElasticDino produces pixel-aligned, high-resolution feature maps efficiently. Leveraging deformations allows strictly preserving sharp semantics, and thereby avoiding the smoothness biases inherent to alternative approaches. Due to the absence of ground truth, we employ pixel-level semantic segmentation and depth estimation with linear heads to predict a set of downstream dense tasks, guiding the deformation process without leaking task-specific semantics into the model. We demonstrate superior accuracy over current methods on a range of popular dense task benchmarks, with better computational performance.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 ElasticDino，一个基于空间变形的轻量适配器，把 ViT 特征上采样为与输入图像像素对齐的高分辨率特征图，并利用伪影跨通道一致的观察同时校正伪影，以线性头在分割与深度任务上验证效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 不涉及 latent 推理或证据获取，但「通道一致伪影同时重对齐」与变形保留锐利语义的机制，可供核查其是否能用于在 LVR 内部状态中维持细粒度视觉细节、避免平滑偏差。
